qs.q: Which southern Mesopotamian city yielded some of the earliest tablets documenting the emergence of writing?

qs.q: What distinguishes the signs that gave cuneiform writing its name?

qs.q: Why did institutions in early Mesopotamian cities need to record goods and services?
qs.why: Early writing involved accounting for goods and services and recording administrative transactions.

qs.q: Which city was Egypt's administrative capital during the Old Kingdom?

qs.q: During which ancient Egyptian dynasty was Djoser's Step Pyramid built?

qs.q: What was the architectural function of the apadana in Achaemenid Persian palaces?

qs.q: Where was a Roman villa usually located compared with urban homes?
qs.why: Roman villas were associated with rural residences and estates.

qs.q: What pattern do Roman facing stones known as opus reticulatum form?
qs.why: The faces of the facing stones are arranged in a regular diagonal grid.

qs.q: What was the main purpose of the Barbegal complex in Roman times?
qs.why: The complex was used to grind grain and produce flour.

qs.q: What power drove the machinery of the Roman Barbegal complex?
qs.why: Water drove the complex's wheels.

qs.q: Who was the last king of the Neo-Babylonian state before Achaemenid rule?
qs.why: The Neo-Babylonian state's rule ended with Nabonidus.

qs.q: What was the architectural function of the Propylaea on the Acropolis?
qs.why: The Propylaea was the main entrance to the Acropolis.

qs.q: Which architect designed the Propylaea of the Acropolis?
qs.why: The Propylaea's design is attributed to Mnesicles.

qs.q: Which sculptor supervised the Parthenon project?
qs.why: Phidias was the sculptor supervising the project.

qs.q: Which shape distinguishes the traditional pediment on Greek architectural facades?
qs.why: A traditional pediment forms a triangular gable above the facade.

qs.q: What is entasis in Greek architectural columns?
choices: A spiral twist in the shaft
A slight convex swelling in the shaft
A square recess in the base
qs.why: Entasis is a slight convex curvature in a column's shaft.

qs.q: From which metal was the Achaemenid siglos coin made?
qs.why: The siglos was a silver coin.

qs.q: How was the Gate of the Sun at Tiwanaku made?
qs.why: The gate was carved from a single stone block.

qs.q: In which Andean country did the Wari civilization flourish?
qs.why: The Wari civilization flourished in parts of Peru.

qs.q: For which technique were decorated Wari tunics known?
qs.why: These tunics were made using tapestry weaving.

qs.q: What did the style known as verism emphasize in Roman portraits?
qs.why: This style depicted realistic facial details and signs of aging.

qs.q: Which Han-era envoy's journeys helped establish contact between China and Central Asia?
qs.why: Zhang Qian traveled as an envoy to Central Asia.

qs.q: What are the panels between triglyphs in a Doric frieze called?
qs.why: Metopes alternate with triglyphs along the frieze.

qs.q: Which decorative feature distinguishes triglyph panels in a Doric frieze?
qs.why: Their grooves run vertically.

qs.q: What is the cavea in Roman theater architecture?
qs.why: The cavea is the audience seating area in the tiers.

qs.q: How did messages advance in the Achaemenid postal system on royal roads?
choices: By relays of messengers at stations
By one messenger traveling the whole route
qs.why: The Achaemenid postal service relied on successive messengers at roadside stations.

qs.q: Near which Chinese city are the ruins of Yinxu?
qs.why: The ruins of Yinxu are near Anyang.

qs.q: For which ancient Egyptian king was the Great Pyramid of Giza built?
qs.why: The Great Pyramid was built as King Khufu's tomb.

qs.q: With which stone was the Great Pyramid faced when built?
qs.why: The Great Pyramid's exterior casing was limestone.

qs.q: Which classical column order traditionally has no separate base in its Greek form?
qs.why: The traditional Greek Doric column has no separate base.

qs.q: In which country is the ancient city of Tiwanaku?
qs.why: The archaeological city of Tiwanaku is in Bolivia.

qs.q: Which city did Sennacherib choose as his Assyrian capital?
qs.why: Sennacherib made Nineveh his capital.

qs.q: What was the base of the traditional Maya numeral system?
qs.why: The Maya numeral system used base twenty.

qs.q: For what purpose did the Greeks mainly use the hydria vessel?
qs.why: The hydria was a vessel for fetching water.

qs.q: Which type of clay is used in making Chinese porcelain?
qs.why: Kaolin is a component of Chinese porcelain.

qs.q: What does the name sancai mean in Chinese ceramics?
qs.why: The name sancai means three colors.

qs.q: Which animal pulled the plow in Mesopotamian agriculture?
qs.why: Oxen were used to pull plows in Mesopotamia.

qs.q: What guidance did inscribed pillars beside Roman roads provide?
qs.why: These pillars indicated distances along roads.

qs.q: Who founded China's Han dynasty?
qs.why: Liu Bang founded the Han dynasty.

qs.q: From which city did the Northern Song dynasty rule?
qs.why: Kaifeng was the Northern Song dynasty's capital.

qs.q: In which country did the Moche civilization arise?
qs.why: The Moche civilization flourished in Peru.

qs.q: For which substance did the Greeks usually use the lekythos vessel?
qs.why: The lekythos was used to hold oil.

qs.q: What covered the roofs of many important buildings in ancient China?
qs.why: Tiles were used to cover these roofs.

qs.q: In which country did the ancient Paracas culture flourish?
qs.why: The Paracas culture flourished in Peru.

qs.q: What did a calpulli refer to in Aztec society?
qs.why: A calpulli was a local community of residents.

qs.q: During which Egyptian dynasty did Tutankhamun rule?
qs.why: Tutankhamun ruled during the Eighteenth Dynasty.

qs.q: What natural event badly damaged Petra in 363 CE?
qs.why: An earthquake in 363 CE damaged many buildings in Petra.

qs.q: How does the size of the famous terracotta soldier statues compare with a human's size?
choices: One and a half times life-size
qs.why: The soldier statues were made at approximately human life-size.

qs.q: Which description applies to the principle of Babylonian numeration?
qs.why: Their system was positional: a sign's value changed according to its position in the number.

qs.q: What kind of room was the caldarium in Roman baths?
qs.why: The caldarium was the hot bathing room.

qs.q: Which shape was common for seals of the Indus civilization?
qs.why: Square seals were common in the Indus civilization.

qs.q: What event helped preserve many Linear B tablets?
qs.why: The clay of many of these tablets hardened when exposed to accidental fires.

qs.q: What type of roofing is known from the tholos tombs at Mycenae?
qs.why: These tombs were roofed with stepped vaulting known as corbeling.

qs.q: What is the nature of signs in the Maya writing system?
qs.why: Maya writing combined word signs with syllabic signs.

qs.q: What was the main building material of Cahokia's great mounds?
qs.why: Cahokia's mounds were built from earth.

qs.q: To which cultural tradition did Cahokia belong during its flourishing period?
qs.why: Cahokia belongs to the Mississippian cultural tradition.

qs.q: What was the function of Cahokia's wooden Woodhenge circle?
qs.why: Sunrise positions helped determine the seasons at Woodhenge.

qs.q: How does boustrophedon writing proceed in some ancient southern Arabian inscriptions?
qs.why: The direction of writing changes from one line to the next.

qs.q: How were dressed blocks secured in the finest Inca stone walls?
qs.why: The precise fit of the dressed blocks made mortar unnecessary.

qs.q: What covered many roofs of Inca buildings?
qs.why: Many roofs were covered with grass bundles.

qs.q: On what surface are pigments applied in ancient true fresco?
qs.why: True fresco pigments are applied to plaster while it is still wet.

qs.q: From which material was the ancient Cyrus Cylinder made?
qs.why: The Cyrus Cylinder was made of clay.

qs.q: What material was used for the ropes of Inca suspension bridges?
qs.why: The ropes were made from braided plant fibers, including grasses.

qs.q: Which policy did the Qin dynasty follow after unifying China?
qs.why: The Qin dynasty standardized writing, currency and measures.

qs.q: What was the usual form of ancient Egyptian papyrus books?
choices: A folded object with alternating folds
A booklet sewn along one side
qs.why: Papyrus sheets were joined to make a long scroll.

qs.q: On what land structure was the Persepolis palace complex built?
choices: A low courtyard beneath the rock
qs.why: The palace complex was built on a broad raised terrace.

qs.q: How did chasquis transport official messages in the Inca state?
choices: Officials collecting them on periodic journeys
Runners taking turns along the route
One runner covering the whole route
qs.why: Runners passed messages along successive stages.

qs.q: Which Athenian reformer reorganized citizens' tribal divisions?
qs.why: Cleisthenes reorganized Athens' tribal structure.

qs.q: What was a common building material for ancient Egyptian homes?
qs.why: Many ancient Egyptian homes were built from mudbrick.

qs.q: Why did carving of the Unfinished Obelisk stop before its removal from the quarry?
choices: The design was changed to a smaller obelisk
There were too few means to transport it to the river
qs.why: Work stopped after cracks appeared in the stone.

qs.q: How were raised designs made in Roman cameo glass?
choices: By pressing designs into a mold
By carving the outer glass layer
By painting pigments onto the surface
qs.why: The outer glass was carved to reveal decoration above a differently colored layer.

qs.q: On what material were many everyday letters written in ancient southern Arabia?
qs.why: Everyday letters were written on wooden sticks.

qs.q: By what other name is the Colosseum amphitheater known?
qs.why: The Colosseum is also known as the Flavian Amphitheater.

qs.q: Which activity was among the main uses of the Roman basilica?
qs.why: Basilica halls were used to hear legal cases.

qs.q: What is the main roof-supporting framework in traditional Chinese architecture?
qs.why: Columns and beams carried the roof in this construction.

qs.q: What was the structural role of dougong in ancient Chinese buildings?
qs.why: Dougong helped support the edges of the roof.

qs.q: Where was the axial rudder mounted on Chinese ships known for this development?
qs.why: This rudder was mounted at the ship's stern.

qs.q: What is the main function of the device known as Archimedes' screw?
qs.why: Archimedes' screw was used to raise water.

qs.q: What was the original practical use of stone palettes in ancient Egypt?
qs.why: Palettes were used to grind cosmetics.

qs.q: What was a common shape of Dilmun stamp seals?
qs.why: Many Dilmun seals were circular.

qs.q: What distinguished the design of the Dujiangyan irrigation system?
choices: Diverting water without a river-blocking dam
Storing water behind a high dam
qs.why: The system diverted river water without a dam blocking its flow.

qs.q: Which Aztec city was famous for its large market?
qs.why: Tlatelolco was famous for its large market.

qs.q: In which country is the archaeological site of Chavin de Huantar?
qs.why: Chavin de Huantar is in Peru.

qs.q: In which Arabian oasis did Babylonian King Nabonidus spend part of his reign?
qs.why: Nabonidus stayed at the Tayma oasis during part of his reign.

qs.q: What structure distinguished the hypocaust heating system in Roman baths?
choices: A heating tank above each room
A floor raised above a heated space
An interior hearth at each room's center
qs.why: Heat from the furnace reached the space beneath the raised floor.

qs.q: What was the source of the water collected by the impluvium basin in a Roman house?
choices: A cistern raised above the house
A city channel connected to the wall
Rain falling through the roof opening
A well dug beneath the atrium
qs.why: The basin collected rainwater falling through the opening in the atrium roof.

qs.q: How did ancient Chinese craftspeople shape jade?
qs.why: Jade was shaped by gradual grinding with abrasive materials.

qs.q: What is the traditional method of making Andean chuno potatoes?
qs.why: Preparing chuno relies on freezing and drying potatoes.

qs.q: Which type of Chinese ceramic transmits some light when thin?
qs.why: Porcelain is translucent when thin.

qs.q: Which Roman technique allowed repeated relief designs on glass vessels?
qs.why: The blown glass took on the designs of the mold's inner surface.

qs.q: Which Roman painting style was known for making walls appear to open onto architectural scenes?
qs.why: The Second Style depicted architecture suggesting that space extended beyond the wall.

qs.q: What were the large walls at Chan Chan mainly built from?
qs.why: The large walls at Chan Chan were built from earth.

qs.q: What role did the agora play in ancient Athenian life?
qs.why: The agora was a center of civic activity in Athens.

qs.q: To which Bronze Age cultural tradition did Tiryns belong?
qs.why: Tiryns was a center of Mycenaean civilization.

qs.q: For which feature was Cyclopean construction in Mycenaean civilization known?
qs.why: Cyclopean construction was distinguished by its massive stone blocks.

qs.q: Which city was Egypt's capital during most of the Eighteenth Dynasty?
qs.why: Thebes was Egypt's capital during most of the Eighteenth Dynasty.

qs.q: In which US state are the ruins of Mesa Verde?
qs.why: The ruins of Mesa Verde are in Colorado.

qs.q: In which US state are the archaeological sites of Chaco Canyon?
qs.why: The archaeological sites of Chaco Canyon are in New Mexico.

qs.q: What is the famous axis around which Teotihuacan's monuments are arranged?
qs.why: The Avenue of the Dead formed a principal axis of the city's plan.

qs.q: Which two elements does the talud-tablero style combine in Teotihuacan architecture?
qs.why: The style combines rectangular panels with sloping sections.

qs.q: Who was the father of Cyrus II, known as Cyrus the Great?
qs.why: Cambyses I was the father of Cyrus the Great.

qs.q: Which alloy was used for crossbow trigger mechanisms in Han China?
qs.why: Bronze was used to make these trigger mechanisms.

qs.q: The ancient name Magan was associated with parts of which present-day country?
qs.why: Ancient Magan included parts of Oman.

qs.q: For which metal was ancient Magan famous?
qs.why: Magan was famous for copper.

qs.q: What was the main purpose of the canal network Sennacherib built around Nineveh?
choices: Supplying water to the city and its surroundings
qs.why: The canals carried water to Nineveh and the surrounding region.
